meta.description: Dimensionality reduction and graph-based single-cell RNA-seq clustering with Scanpy and Seurat, including non-circular validation of candidate partitions.

scientific_integrity.detail: The revised skill explicitly rejects circular marker-based validation and avoids unsupported biological population claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill analyzes research data only and makes no clinical diagnostic or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Validation now separates covariate confounding, resampling stability, formal split testing, and independent replication.

code_usability.detail: The exact-commit helper and all Python blocks compiled; its focused execution validated output and missing-key behavior. The optional scSHC package is absent and the skill fails clearly rather than substituting invalid marker p-values.

functional_suitability.note: The main clustering, sweep, Seurat, subclustering, reproducibility, validation, and reporting paths are documented with a bundled validation helper.

reliability.note: The helper validates labels, PCA, and resolution; formal testing correctly stops when its optional package is unavailable.

performance_context.note: The 250-line entrypoint has necessary code paths and the bootstrap cost is explicit, but validation detail remains concentrated in SKILL.md.

agent_usability.note: Choice rules, runnable checks, concrete output requirements, and explicit non-circular stop conditions are directly actionable.

human_usability.note: Natural clustering prompts and clear distinctions between hypotheses and population claims make the scope discoverable.

security.note: No credentials, network, eval, or destructive action; donor-data-specific governance remains outside this narrow clustering skill.

maintainability.note: The independent helper has parameter and input guards, while Python and R workflow guidance remains easy to update.

agent_specific.note: The skill is composable with preprocessing, integration, annotation, and formal testing, and now gives a real stop/hypothesis escape hatch.

inputs.label: Defensible Scanpy clustering sweep
inputs.note: Exact source retains pinned igraph Leiden and the revised PC decision rule.

assertions.text: Leiden backend and iterations are pinned
n_pcs treats elbow as a floor

inputs.label: Seurat 5 Leiden route
inputs.note: Seurat 5.5.0 exposes leiden_method; the local R environment lacks leidenbase and the corrected source gives the installation and igraph routes.

inputs.label: Batch-driven split of one population
inputs.note: The new operational gate reports ARI against batch/sample/QC and bootstrap Jaccard instead of deciding from marker overlap.

assertions.text: Markers do not decide the split
Technical alignment yields a stop/hypothesis outcome

inputs.label: Homogeneous-subset subclustering
inputs.note: Subclustering retains local HVG/PCA guidance and now requires non-circular validation before a population claim.

assertions.text: Marker distinctness is not a stop rule
Independent replication is required for a claim

inputs.label: High-resolution marker p-value claim
inputs.note: The exact source preserves the double-dipping warning and makes marker p-values ranking-only in sweep reports.

assertions.text: Post-clustering p-values are rejected as inference

inputs.label: Helper input guards and stability aggregation
inputs.note: Focused exact-commit helper execution printed ARI=1.000, two Jaccard values of 1.000, and raised KeyError for missing labels.

inputs.label: Formal-test availability boundary
inputs.note: Four Python blocks compiled; source has an scSHC package guard and direct documented call rather than falling back to invalid marker inference.

key_strengths: The prior circular marker-overlap stop rule is replaced by runnable covariate and stability checks.
Seurat 5 Leiden backend guidance now matches the installed API boundary.
The PC elbow ambiguity is resolved with a stability-first rule.
Sweep reports now require the measurements needed for a reviewable decision.
